blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: A Deployment keeps identical Pods running. It comes from the apps/v1 API.
blocks.why: This one also says which nodes its Pods may run on.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: What to create: a Deployment, from the apps/v1 API

blocks.title: Give it a name
blocks.why: Imagine an app that needs fast SSD disks, so it must run on SSD nodes.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: A name to find the Deployment
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ssd-web

blocks.title: Two copies and their label
blocks.what: Keep two Pods running, and manage the Pods labelled app: ssd-web.
blocks.why: Two copies show that every Pod follows the same node rule.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because apps/v1 Deployments must have a selector.
blocks.comment: Two copies of the Pods that carry this label
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ssd-web
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: ssd-web

blocks.title: Describe the Pods
blocks.what: The template is the blueprint for each Pod. It gives each Pod the selector’s label.
blocks.why: The template labels must match the selector, as in every Deployment.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Deployment would have nothing to create, so Kubernetes rejects it.
blocks.comment: The blueprint for each Pod, with the label the selector looks for
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ssd-web
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: ssd-web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ssd-web

blocks.title: Rules for choosing a node
blocks.what: nodeAffinity lists rules about node labels. required… means the scheduler must follow them.
blocks.why: IgnoredDuringExecution means Pods already running stay put if a node’s labels change later.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Pods can run on any node.
blocks.comment: The scheduler must follow these node rules when placing a Pod
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ssd-web
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: ssd-web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ssd-web
    spec:
      affinity:
        nodeAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            nodeSelectorTerms:

blocks.title: Only SSD nodes
blocks.what: The rule matches nodes whose disktype label is In the list: ssd.
blocks.why: Labels describe nodes, such as disk type or zone. The rule picks nodes by them.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Deployment, because the rule list cannot be empty.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ssd-web
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: ssd-web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ssd-web
    spec:
      affinity:
        nodeAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            nodeSelectorTerms:
              - matchExpressions:
                  - key: disktype
                    operator: In
                    values:
                      - ssd

blocks.title: What should run?
blocks.what: Each Pod runs one nginx container. This block makes the file ready.
blocks.why: Until a node has the label, the Pods wait in Pending.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Deployment, because its Pods would have nothing to run.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ssd-web
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: ssd-web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ssd-web
    spec:
      affinity:
        nodeAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            nodeSelectorTerms:
              - matchExpressions:
                  - key: disktype
                    operator: In
                    values:
                      - ssd
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: nginx:1.30.4

notes.apiVersion: The API group and version that define this kind. Deployments are in apps/v1.
notes.kind: The type of object to create. A Deployment keeps identical Pods running.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.metadata.name: The Deployment’s name. Its Pods get names that start with it.
notes.spec: The desired state of the Deployment.
notes.spec.replicas: How many Pods to keep running.
notes.spec.selector: Which Pods this Deployment manages. It cannot change after creation.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels: Pods must have all of these labels to be managed by this Deployment.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels.app: Match Pods whose app label is ssd-web.
notes.spec.template: The Pod template: the blueprint for every Pod this Deployment creates.
notes.spec.template.metadata: Details given to every Pod created from the template.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels: Labels given to every Pod. They must match the selector.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels.app: Every Pod gets the label app: ssd-web, so the selector finds it.
notes.spec.template.spec: What each Pod runs. This is the same spec as in a Pod file.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers: The containers in each Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].name: The container’s name. It must be unique within the Pod.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].image: The nginx web server, pinned to a version.
notes.spec.template.spec.affinity: Rules that attract Pods to nodes, or keep them near or apart from other Pods.
notes.spec.template.spec.affinity.nodeAffinity: Rules about which nodes the Pods may run on, based on node labels.
Hard rules: a Pod waits in Pending until a node matches. Running Pods are never moved.
A list of choices. A node that matches any one of them is allowed.
Conditions a node must meet. A node must match all of them.
The node label to look at: disktype.
In: the label’s value must be one of the values below. NotIn and Exists also work.
The allowed values for the label.
ssd: only nodes with disktype=ssd match.

tryIt.result: Both Pods show Pending. No node has the disktype=ssd label yet.
Each Pod’s event says the nodes didn’t match Pod’s node affinity/selector.
Lists the three nodes. Pick one name for the next commands.

check.run: kubectl label node $(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') disktype=ssd

tryIt.result: Both Pods are Running, and the NODE column shows the node you labelled.

check.run: kubectl get pods -l app=ssd-web --field-selector spec.nodeName=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}'),status.phase=Running -o name

tryIt.result: The dash removes the label. Prints node/<node> unlabeled.

check.run: kubectl label node $(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') disktype-

tryIt.result: Both Pods keep running. The rule is only checked when a Pod is placed.
Removes the Deployment and its Pods.

questions.question: No node has the label disktype=ssd. What happens to the Pods?
questions.explain: A required rule is never relaxed. The Pods wait until a node matches.

questions.question: You remove the label from the node the Pods run on. What happens?
answers: The Pods are stopped at once
The Pods move to another node
questions.explain: IgnoredDuringExecution: the rule only counts when a Pod is placed.

questions.question: Which operator would keep the Pods off SSD nodes instead?
questions.explain: NotIn allows any node whose label is not in the list.

fix.message: The Deployment "ssd-web" is invalid: spec.template.spec.affinity.nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.nodeSelectorTerms[0].matchExpressions[0].operator: Invalid value: "in": not a valid selector operator
fix.explain: Operators are case-sensitive. Kubernetes knows In, but not in.
fix.fix: Write the operator with a capital I: In.

sources.title: Assign Pods to Nodes using Node Affinity
